issues.legal_issue: A final determination of entitlement in an earlier suit between the same parties bars relitigation of that issue in a later suit, notwithstanding an observation that the earlier judgment would not prevent a suit for possession.
material_facts: An earlier suit sought permanent injunction concerning management and possession of the Gaddi.
The earlier courts determined that the claimant was not entitled to hold or manage the Gaddi, and the Supreme Court restored the appellate decree containing those findings.
A later suit between the parties sought possession of the properties on the basis of entitlement to the Gaddi.
The earlier Supreme Court judgment stated that it would not come in the way of filing a suit for possession, if the claimant was so advised.
issues.conclusion: The earlier determination of entitlement was final and binding, and the later suit was barred by res judicata; the observation about filing a suit for possession did not remove that bar.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure bars a matter directly and substantially in issue that was heard and finally decided in a former suit between the same parties litigating under the same title before a competent court; Explanation IV extends the bar to matters that might and ought to have been raised. Section 12 addresses suits barred by res judicata. Order II Rule 2 bars a second suit for relief that could but was not claimed in the first suit. A judgment is read in the context of its facts, and an observation does not override the applicable law or the binding ratio. The court relied on Sheodan Singh v. Daryao Kunwar, State of U.P. v. Nawab Hussain, Home Plantations Ltd. v. Talaku Land Board, Fateh Singh v. Jagannath Baksh Singh, and Shiv Kumar Sharma v. Santosh Kumari.

rule.if: later_possession_suit and same_parties and prior_entitlement_issue_decided_finally and prior_court_competent and (prior_observation_allows_fresh_suit or not prior_observation_allows_fresh_suit)

predicates.later_possession_suit: A party brought a later suit seeking possession of property.
predicates.same_parties: The parties to the later suit were the same as, or claimed under, the parties to the earlier suit and litigated under the same title.
predicates.prior_entitlement_issue_decided_finally: The earlier suit directly and substantially raised the parties’ competing entitlement, and that issue was heard and finally decided.
predicates.prior_court_competent: The court deciding the earlier suit was competent to decide the issue and the later suit.
predicates.prior_observation_allows_fresh_suit: The earlier judgment included an observation that a party could bring a fresh suit for possession.
predicates.not_prior_observation_allows_fresh_suit: The earlier judgment did not include an observation that a party could bring a fresh suit for possession.

issues.definition: When a later suit for possession between the same parties raises an entitlement issue finally decided by a competent court in the earlier suit, that issue bars the later suit, whether or not the earlier judgment included an observation allowing a fresh suit.

issues.legal_issue: A contempt proceeding should not be initiated when no specific ground for doing so is established at that stage.
material_facts: A contempt petition was before the Court alongside the civil appeal.
The Court found no specific ground to initiate contempt proceedings at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to initiate contempt proceedings in the absence of a specific ground; no statutory provision or earlier case was relied upon for this disposition.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding asking the court to address alleged contempt.
predicates.no_specific_ground_to_initiate_contempt: The court found no specific ground to initiate contempt proceedings at that stage.

issues.definition: A contempt proceeding is dismissed when the court finds no specific ground to initiate contempt proceedings at that stage.
